In [[mathematics]], the '''Arason invariant''' is a [[cohomological invariant]] associated to a [[quadratic form]] of even rank and trivial [[Discriminant#Discriminant of a quadratic form|discriminant]] and [[Clifford invariant]] over a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] ''k'' of [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] not 2, taking values in H<sup>3</sup>(''k'','''Z'''/2'''Z'''). It was introduced by Jón Arason in 1975.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Arason |first=Jón Kr |date=September 1975 |title=Cohomologische invarianten quadratischer Formen |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0021869375901453 |journal=Journal of Algebra |language=de |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=448–491 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(75)90145-3|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The [[Rost invariant]] is a generalization of the Arason invariant to other algebraic groups.

==Definition==

Suppose that ''W''(''k'') is the [[Witt ring (forms)|Witt ring]] of quadratic forms over a field ''k'' and ''I'' is the ideal of forms of even dimension. The Arason invariant is a [[group homomorphism]] from ''I''<sup>3</sup> to the [[Galois cohomology]] group H<sup>3</sup>(''k'','''Z'''/2'''Z'''). It is determined by the property that on the 8-dimensional diagonal form with entries 1, –''a'', –''b'', ''ab'', -''c'', ''ac'', ''bc'', -''abc'' (the 3-fold [[Pfister form]]«''a'',''b'',''c''») it is given by the [[cup product]] of the classes of ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' in H<sup>1</sup>(''k'','''Z'''/2'''Z''') = ''k''*/''k''*<sup>2</sup>. The Arason invariant vanishes on ''I''<sup>4</sup>, and it follows from the [[Milnor conjecture (K-theory)|Milnor conjecture]] proved by Voevodsky that it is an [[Group isomorphism|isomorphism]] from ''I''<sup>3</sup>/''I''<sup>4</sup> to H<sup>3</sup>(''k'','''Z'''/2'''Z''').
